title: 2027 French presidential election: Parties torn between internal rivalry and unity against radical options
subhead: Given the electoral momentum of the far right and radical left, the prospect of a single candidate is now a pressing question on the left, centrist and right-wing blocs. Moderate voters may be tempted to cast a strategic vote in the first round for the candidate most likely to prevent a dreaded runoff between Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

title: Tibet landslide undermines Xi Jinping's gamble on the Himalayas
subhead: The devastated Gyirong border post stands at the heart of China's strategy for south Asia. A railway line, set to become a key link in the Belt and Road Initiative, is planned to pass through here.

subhead: European leaders gave a reserved response after Iceland voted against resuming accession talks, a result welcomed by far-right Euroskeptic parties.

title: 'No regulation exists:' Suez Canal becomes gateway for invasive species in the Mediterranean
subhead: 'Suez, a historic canal' (6/6). The opening of a passage between the Red Sea and the Mediterranean led to migrations of 'Lessepsian' species, named after the canal's developer, Ferdinand de Lesseps. Their proliferation, which destabilizes ecosystems, has increased due to overfishing, pollution, coastal building and climate change.

title: Will this summer's climate disasters push French politicians and citizens to act?

title: The hunt for musketeer d'Artagnan's tomb sparks archaeological row
subhead: Archaeologist Wim Dijkman uncovered a skeleton in a church in the Netherlands that could belong to the famous French musketeer. The municipality accused him of carrying out illegal excavations and took the project away from him. It will take a few more months before the DNA analysis reveals its secrets.
